topic: npm ci vs npm install in CI: reproducible installs from the lockfile, and failing on drift
text:
Your CI can ship different dependencies than the ones you tested locally, and nobody notices.

The cause is often one word: `npm install` in the pipeline. Per the npm docs, it can update package-lock.json. `npm ci` never writes package.json or the lockfile.

What npm ci does:
• needs an existing package-lock.json
• exits with an error if the lockfile and package.json disagree
• deletes node_modules first, so every build starts clean
• installs the whole project, not single packages

That error is the feature. A lockfile that drifted from package.json gets caught in the PR, not in production.

My rule of thumb: npm install on your laptop when you change dependencies, npm ci in CI and Docker builds, and commit the lockfile.

Does your pipeline fail on lockfile drift today, or does it quietly fix it?
